about.title: Anderson Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Anderson residents rely on local clinics, urgent care centers, and hospitals throughout Shasta County for everything from routine checkups to emergency treatment. Most visits go fine, but when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mishandles medication, the consequences can follow a patient for years. Medical malpractice cases are different from other injury claims — California's MICRA law requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in, strict notice deadlines apply, and there's a cap on non-economic damages that changes annually. A bad outcome by itself isn't enough to prove malpractice; the law requires showing the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we're a free service that connects Anderson residents with an independent attorney who can review the medical records, evaluate whether a provider fell short, and explain what options may exist within California's specific rules for these claims.

whyChoose.title: Why This Process Matters Under California Law

items.title: Strict Notice and Filing Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires a claim within one year of discovering the injury and no more than three years from when it occurred, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because MICRA requires a qualified medical expert to support most malpractice claims, an early case evaluation helps determine whether the medical records show a deviation from the standard of care rather than just an unfortunate outcome.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises Yearly
items.desc: California law places a statutory limit on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap increases annually. An independent attorney can walk through how this framework may apply to your specific circumstances.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery in Anderson — does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. An independent attorney typically arranges for a qualified medical expert to review the records before drawing any conclusions.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after discovering a medical error?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice period before filing suit, so earlier review is generally better than later.

items.question: Do I need to find a malpractice attorney based in Shasta County specifically?
Do I need an attorney located in Shasta County to handle an Anderson case?
items.answer: Not necessarily — what matters more is experience with California's malpractice rules and access to the right medical experts for your type of claim.
